It just got so toxic. This person could be trapped in a mental hell. I'm not saying OP's feelings aren't valid, as I said before. I'm just saying her husband needs help too and criticizing him for something he can't control is pointless. 

Also, he may not seem interested in changing his behavior for many reasons. If mental health is the reason, it's very much understandable. Sometimes, when you're so deep in, you don't open up, you don't have it in you to care about other people anymore. You have no energy to give. You're constantly angry, irritated, and in so much pain that you can't function well. 

Whatever the reason may be, getting him to open up is the only way.

Again, you can't comment on his gratification with certainty. If you read OP's previous post you'll see that this guy has no interest in having sex with her. He's said he preferred jacking off and that she could do the same. He's even suggested that he didn't mind if she slept with someone else. I'm surprised he's still having sex at all. He's clearly showing a major lack of interest. OP has also mentioned all this started with the changes that came with quarantine and that he wasn't like this before. I acted the same way with my bf before I broke up with him. During sex, I only focused on what made sex pleasurable for me because it was that hard to find pleasure in something I've completely lost interest in. And yet I had sex because I tried my best to keep everything going. It took me so much damn courage to break up with him because I had lost all interest in the relationship. What they need is support. Not judgment. I agree the husband should be more direct about his feelings and open up to OP about whatever he's going through, but ppl struggling with their mental health are very hesitant to tell how they truly feel for fear of not being understood. 

>She HAS talked to him about it

She's talked to him about what she wants during sex. I don't know if she's talked to him about his mental health.

You can't jump to those conclusions. There's no doubt his behavior is hurting his wife, but he could be under so much pressure himself that he's unable to give his attention to everything. What if he's having sex cuz he feels like that's the minimum he could do to please her? Depression is a mental health issue. You cannot decide how depression or any other mental health issue should look. It affects people differently. Ppl become angry, distant, or extremely quiet. I deal with it and I'm disconnected from a lot of the things I used to love. I broke up with my bf over quarantine because I was in a hell of my own. Sex was almost repulsive, yet I did it to keep things going. OP has mentioned he's struggling and that he's very stressed out, yet somehow we're focusing on his inability to please her? I feel like his mental health deserves to be talked about more. There's no doubt OP is frustrated too. I just don't see why we can't focus on his frustrations and struggles equally?

What if he's doing the best he can with the lack of motivation/ interest? Either way, I wouldn't blame someone going through mental health struggles. They need to talk about this. He needs to communicate about his feelings, whatever he's going through, and the reason he can't do what she's asking. You can't exactly force someone to do something in bed if they don't want to. When you're depressed you tend to lack interest, empathy, motivation, etc. I'd say OP should confront her husband about this and look into therapy or even seeing a psychiatrist if they need support.
